knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Radical Function Using the Chain Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=5x-1.$ Then $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}={u}^{-1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-3/2}=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=5.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}\cdot (5) \\  & =-\frac{5}{2\sqrt{(5x-1{)}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{1-4x}$ at the point where $x=-2.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=1-4x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (-4) \\  & =-\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-4x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-2} & ={(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-4x}})|}_{x=-2} \\  & =\frac{-4}{2\sqrt{1-4(-2)}} \\  & =\frac{-4}{2\sqrt{9}} \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: The slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3{x}^{2}+12x}}$ at the point where $x=2$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=3{x}^{2}+12x.$ Then $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}={u}^{-1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-3/2}=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x+12.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}\cdot (6x+12) \\  & =-\frac{6x+12}{2\sqrt{(3{x}^{2}+12x{)}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=2} & ={(-\frac{6x+12}{2\sqrt{(3{x}^{2}+12x{)}^{3}}})|}_{x=2} \\  & =-\frac{6(2)+12}{2\sqrt{(3(2{)}^{2}+12(2){)}^{3}}} \\  & =-\frac{24}{2\sqrt{{36}^{3}}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: The slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{3{x}^{2}+2x}$ at the point where $x=-1$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=3{x}^{2}+2x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x+2.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (6x+2) \\  & =\frac{2(3x+1)}{2\sqrt{3{x}^{2}+2x}} \\  & =\frac{3x+1}{\sqrt{3{x}^{2}+2x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-1} & ={(\frac{3x+1}{\sqrt{3{x}^{2}+2x}})|}_{x=-1} \\  & =\frac{6(-1)+2}{2\sqrt{3(-1{)}^{2}+2(-1)}} \\  & =\frac{-4}{2\sqrt{1}} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(-\frac{x-1}{\sqrt{-{x}^{2}+2x}})|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{2-2(1)}{2\sqrt{-(1{)}^{2}+2(1)}} \\  & =\frac{0}{2\sqrt{1}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

Let $u=-{x}^{2}+2x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$

$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-2x+2.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (-2x+2) \\  & =\frac{-2x+2}{2\sqrt{-{x}^{2}+2x}}.\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{x-3}+3{x}^{3}$ at the point where $x=4.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Let $f(x)=\sqrt{x-3}.$ We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=x-3.$ Then $f=\sqrt{u}={u}^{1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-1/2}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x-3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the sum rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x-3}}+9x^{2}.
$$

Finally, substituting $x=4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=4} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{(4)-3}}+9(4)^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+144 \\  & =\frac{289}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{3{x}^{2}+24}$ at the point where $x=-2.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=3{x}^{2}+24.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (6x) \\  & =\frac{6x}{2\sqrt{3{x}^{2}+24}} \\  & =\frac{3x}{\sqrt{3{x}^{2}+24}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-2} & ={(\frac{3x}{\sqrt{3{x}^{2}+24}})|}_{x=-2} \\  & =\frac{6(-2)}{2\sqrt{3(-2{)}^{2}+24}} \\  & =\frac{-12}{2\sqrt{36}} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
